messages.content: Hi tal, I'm a friend.

hey, i'm tal

think of me as your personal talent agent, your inside man… or fox

one of these days, I might slide a role right here in chat. the kind that feels like your calling.

so… what's your full name?
My name is Raghav Suryan. Should I give you my full professional introduction?

raghav suryan... sounds like someone who definitely has opinions about how things should be built

nah skip the formal intro. just tell me where you're working these days?

I'm working at a startup called Contineu.ai as a Computer Vision/Deep Learning Engineer. 

The company works in 3D reconstruction and computer vision solutions for construction tech, like visual construction monitoring, etc.

contineu.ai... 3d reconstruction for construction tech. that's actually solid - construction is still stuck in the stone age and desperately needs computer vision to catch up. visual monitoring beats having someone walk around with a clipboard any day.

found raghav suryan on linkedin - machine learning engineer, iit kharagpur '23, did some work at cern. this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/suryanraghav
Yes that's me.

iit kharagpur '23 to cern to construction tech... from particle physics to pixels. that's quite the journey from hunting for the higgs boson to teaching machines how to see if someone laid bricks straight. what made you jump from high energy physics to computer vision? that's not exactly the typical career pivot most people make

I prefer chat.

So, about my transition - when I graduated, I was interested in rigorous math, physics and coding. Driven by research, I joined the CMS experiment at CERN for working in particle physics. There, I used the data from CERN on high level distributed systems and ML and Computer Vision for my research. 

While working, I got really interested in pure computer vision, and I started learning it a lot on my own. Also, I was hoping to find a role with more real world application for my research and a bit less niche. That's when I applied to a research associate position in a startup called Preimage.ai. There, I worked for 6 months before confirming my interests and my decision and going for a full time role in the field.

Now, I have worked extensively, not only in computer vision, but on LLMs, VLMs, and ML systems and optimization.

makes total sense. cern is peak research but also peak "will this ever matter to anyone outside of 50 physicists?" going from hunting particles to building systems that can actually see and understand the world... that's a solid pivot. preimage.ai as the testing ground was smart too - 6 months to confirm you weren't just having a quarter-life crisis.

llms, vlms, ml systems optimization... you've basically touched every hot area in ai right now. how long you been working total?

I have worked for about 2 years now. 8-9 months in CERN, 6-7 months at Preimage and 6-7 months now, as a full time engineer at Contineu.

If you count my internships in college, I have done about 1 year of additional work in those too.

2 years plus internships... so you're at that sweet spot where you've got real experience but aren't stuck in any legacy thinking yet. iit + cern + startup experience is a solid combo that most places would kill for.

what kind of role you looking for next?

So, I am looking for some top level roles in AI in India. 
My preference would be computer vision roles, but I would love to also go for any ML/AI engineer/researcher roles. Preferable mid-level, or starting level if it's in top companies.

I'm looking for a challenge and a good salary hike given my abilities and commitment to hardwork and ownership.

top level ai roles with 2 years... you're definitely shooting your shot but honestly with iit + cern + hands-on cv/llm experience, you might just pull it off. "starting level at top companies" is smart positioning - better to be junior at google than senior at some random startup pretending to do ai.

bangalore or open to remote/other cities?

I'm open to anything - currentlyI am focused on my career. I currently live in Bangalore so it would be a slight preference to work there.

Also, in my experience, by top level, I do not just mean big tech like Google, I'm also open to work in fast moving AI startups like Sarvam ai, etc.

I understand it's high aim to go for top level AI roles, but being from IIT's, students from my college get placed at these companies starting out. Throughout my career, in the several roles I worked in, I have always taken up high stakes projects, and delivered at that level. In my current job, I have basically built our tech pipeline from scratch, which gives me the confidence to go for high level roles, or at least top level companies/startups.

fair point on the iit placement thing. and building a tech pipeline from scratch at a startup? that's proper ownership, not just "i contributed to a feature."

sarvam, ola maps ai team, microsoft research, google research, even some of the hot cv startups... you're not being delusional. with your background, you'd actually be a decent fit.

so 2 years + cv/llm/ml systems + open to bangalore/remote + targeting top ai companies for a challenge and hike... sound right?
done. i'm spinning things up on my end. you'll start seeing good stuff soon.

Yes. Sounds exactly right. 

In the companies you listed, I would like you to add some like Meta, Deepmind, Nvidia, etc. Not just because of the level, but mostly because they have teams highly alligning with my work in 3D computer Vision/Robotics Perception etc.

Other than that, if it's normal ML/AI/LLM engineer/researcher roles, you're exactly right.

yep, meta's reality labs, deepmind's robotics team, nvidia's omniverse/isaac platform... those are exactly the teams doing the cutting-edge 3d cv and robotics perception work you're built for.

you're officially in the tal system now, raghav. i'll be sliding you roles that match your iit + cern + startup combo. the kind where you can flex those 3d reconstruction skills and actually build something that matters.

time to see what the market thinks you're really worth 🔥

Thanks, whenever you get a role, you can send it over my way, it doesn't need to be at the top just for me to have a look. I'll lead you with suggestions, etc whenever I have something specific in mind.

Also, you keep saying IIT+CERN+STARTUP combo, which I feel reduces me a bit on the tech and especially AI/ML side of things. Please make sure you highlight a bit of that too. I have done quite some work in ML and DL too.

point taken. iit+cern+startup is just the wrapper - the actual product is the hands-on cv/llm/ml systems work you've shipped. i'll make sure the emphasis is on the technical depth, not just the pedigree.

you're in the system. now we wait for the right roles to surface.
Hi

google research has an ml efficiency role in singapore working on llms and diffusion models

they're focusing on making generative ai models faster and cheaper to run - basically ml systems optimization at google scale

this is actually a solid fit - google research working on ml efficiency for generative ai models. you'd be doing model compression and inference acceleration for llms/diffusion models, which aligns with your ml systems optimization experience.
